props.doc:
The SDK contract, as a schema.

Every command - platform, HTTP-built or hand-written Python - declares the
same fields. That is what lets the AI reason about the catalogue, the
validator type-check a playbook before publish, and the UI build a form for
a command it has never seen.
props.name: command_contract

props.code:
return {
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["key", "name", "kind", "input_schema", "output_schema",
                 "risk_level", "effect", "trust_level"],
    "additionalProperties": False,
    "properties": {
        "key": {"type": "string", "pattern": "^[a-z0-9_]+\\.[a-z0-9_]+$"},
        "name": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1},
        "category": {"type": "string"},
        "kind": {"enum": ["builtin", "http", "python", "transform", "shell"]},
        "input_schema": {"type": "object"},
        "output_schema": {"type": "object"},
        "implementation": {"type": "object"},
        "auth": {"type": "array", "items": {
            "type": "object", "required": ["role", "credential"],
            "properties": {"role": {"type": "string"},
                           "credential": {"type": "string"}}}},
        "required_permissions": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
        "required_capabilities": {"type": "array", "items": {
            "enum": ["net", "fs.read", "fs.write", "process", "env"]}},
        "timeout_ms": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 100, "maximum": 900000},
        "risk_level": {"enum": ["low", "medium", "high"]},
        "effect": {"enum": ["read", "mutating"]},
        "trust_level": {"enum": ["trusted", "verified", "untrusted"]},
        "dry_run_example": {"type": "object"},
        "retryable_errors": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
        "technique_ids": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
        # The command that undoes this one. Named, never inferred - and
        # declared here because cmd() sets it, the catalogue test asserts it
        # resolves, and the contract refused it, so no connector that named
        # an undo could be installed at all.
        "undo_command": {"type": "string"},
        "doc": {"type": "string"},
    },
}

props.doc: Publish an immutable, content-hashed command version. Trust promotion is a separate, separately-permissioned action; publishing never raises a trust level.
props.name: publish_version

props.code:
from soar.audit.log import record as audit_record
from soar.identity.rbac import require_permission
from soar.platform.ids import new_id

import hashlib
import json

require_permission(principal, "commands.create")
org_id = principal["org_id"]

problems = validate_definition(definition)
if problems:
    raise ValueError("; ".join(problems))

canonical = json.dumps(definition, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
digest = hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).digest()
version_id = new_id("cmdv")

db.execute(
    "INSERT INTO command_version (id, command_id, version, state, kind, "
    "input_schema, output_schema, implementation, required_permissions, "
    "required_capabilities, auth, timeout_ms, risk_level, effect, "
    "content_sha256, created_by, published_at, published_by) "
    "SELECT %s, %s, coalesce(max(version), 0) + 1, 'published', %s, %s, %s, %s, "
    "%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, now(), %s "
    "FROM command_version WHERE command_id = %s",
    [
        version_id, command_id, definition["kind"],
        json.dumps(definition["input_schema"]),
        json.dumps(definition["output_schema"]),
        json.dumps(definition.get("implementation", {})),
        definition.get("required_permissions", []),
        definition.get("required_capabilities", []),
        json.dumps(definition.get("auth", [])),
        definition.get("timeout_ms", 30000),
        definition["risk_level"], definition["effect"], digest,
        principal.get("id"), principal.get("id"), command_id,
    ],
    org_id,
)
db.execute(
    "UPDATE command SET current_version_id = %s WHERE id = %s",
    [version_id, command_id], org_id,
)
audit_record(db, {
    "org_id": org_id, "actor_kind": "user", "actor_id": principal.get("id"),
    "action": "command.publish", "target_kind": "command", "target_id": command_id,
    "after": {"version_id": version_id, "sha256": digest.hex()}, "result": "success",
})
return version_id

props.doc:
Raise a command from untrusted to verified, or to trusted.

Explicit, permissioned, reviewed and audited. Never automatic, and never
inferred from the command having run successfully - "it worked before" is
exactly what a malicious command is designed to look like.
props.name: promote_trust

props.code:
from soar.audit.log import record as audit_record
from soar.identity.rbac import require_permission

ORDER = ["untrusted", "verified", "trusted"]
require_permission(principal, "commands.promote")
org_id = principal["org_id"]

if new_level not in ORDER:
    raise ValueError("unknown trust level")
if new_level == "trusted":
    raise PermissionError(
        "the trusted level is for platform-provided commands only; "
        "use verified for reviewed custom commands"
    )
if not (review_notes or "").strip():
    raise ValueError("a promotion needs review notes; the reviewer is on the record")

rows = db.query(
    "SELECT trust_level, created_by FROM command WHERE id = %s AND org_id = %s",
    [command_id, org_id], org_id,
)
if not rows:
    raise KeyError("no such command")
current = rows[0]["trust_level"]

# Separation of duty: the author does not review their own command.
if rows[0]["created_by"] == principal.get("id"):
    raise PermissionError("a command cannot be promoted by its own author")

db.execute("UPDATE command SET trust_level = %s WHERE id = %s",
           [new_level, command_id], org_id)
audit_record(db, {
    "org_id": org_id, "actor_kind": "user", "actor_id": principal.get("id"),
    "action": "command.trust.promote", "target_kind": "command",
    "target_id": command_id, "before": {"trust_level": current},
    "after": {"trust_level": new_level}, "reason": review_notes, "result": "success",
})
